There’s also a solid chance that they need to encourage online spending, because when the sky turns grey the high-street looks as inviting as wet socks.

Here we round up the best bank holiday reductions on products our testers love, including autumn essentials such as dehumidifiers, duvets and women’s walking boots. As ever when scouring for deals, we’ve used price-checking tools such as PriceRunner and Idealo to check price histories, compare retailers and ensure that all these deals are the real … deal.

One of the easiest kitchen plastic detox swaps you can make is to ditch your two-tone sponges for a compostable alternative. Seep’s dishwasher-safe sponges, made from loofah and wood pulp cellulose, have been recommended many times in the Filter, including in Hannah Rochell’s 12 sustainable cleaning subscriptions and Juliet Kinsman’s 13 ways to make your bathroom more sustainable. This deal gives you 25% off a whole year’s stash (12 sponges).

articles.title: How have my plants fared this summer? Some better than others
articles.summary: It’ll soon be autumn, but the record-breaking weather has taken its toll on my vegetables. I’ve grown plants in heatwaves before, but this year has been different. Back-to-back heatwaves feel far more intense than the shorter ones I’m used to.
body: You might think more sun equals more growth, but that isn’t necessarily the case. When under heat stress, plants close their stomata – the pores on the underside of their leaves – hindering the movement of water and exchange of gases needed for photosynthesis. This can result in a check on growth that I’ve seen in several of my plants, some of which dropped their flowers before they could start bearing fruit.

Stressed-out plants can be vulnerable to pest attacks, which might explain why so many leaf miners have found my chard this year. Even some established perennials have struggled in the heat. The golden raspberries, which are in their second season, had canes that were growing well then suddenly turned brown and died.

articles.title: Cocktail of the week: Legare’s mini bay leaf martini – recipe | The good mixer
articles.summary: Make a batch of this vodka- and vermouth-infused tipple to keep fresh in the fridge and sip over the weeks ahead. We came up with this when we were looking to create some fun, bespoke but easy-to-serve cocktails that we could pre-batch for busy services but that still had an edge.
body: First make the infusion by steeping the bay leaves in the vodka for 10-plus days. Fine-strain, ideally through muslin, into a clean bottle, seal and store in the fridge for up to a month (or almost indefinitely in the freezer).
To make the batch serve, pour the bay-infused vodka into a clean large jug, then add the dry vermouth and filtered water.
To serve, pour 50ml of the mix into chilled mini-martini glasses and garnish each one with an olive.

articles.title: Experience: I brought a bear back to life
articles.summary: I was in India, performing dentistry on my first animal patient, and it was supposed to be a straightforward operation. I’ve been a dentist for 40 years. I spend most of my time treating patients at my surgery in Chichester, West Sussex.
body: Twenty years later, in 2000, that changed. A patient of mine, Alan Knight, the CEO of International Animal Rescue (IAR), showed me photographs of the inside of a bear’s mouth. The bear was called Jojo and his teeth had been broken off by poachers. Some of the teeth were too rotten to be saved – if left untreated, Jojo would become more prone to infection and abscesses.

Alan told me Jojo wasn’t the only bear in need of dental care. Poachers would kill mother bears and grab their cubs. When the cubs got older, the poachers would break their teeth using a hammer to make them look more docile. I knew I had to help.

That was how I ended up in India ready to perform dentistry on my first animal patient – a 14-year-old sloth bear named Anthony. He had a massive benign tumour on his gum that was preventing him from eating. He was 180kg, which is especially big for an Indian sloth bear, and already anaesthetised when I first saw him.

It was supposed to be a relatively straightforward operation – remove the tumour and any bad teeth. I was working alongside a veterinary dentist, Lisa Milella. We’d prepared for over a year – I felt ready.

articles.title: How Does Harry Styles’s Madison Square Garden Show Grow?
articles.summary: Harry, Harry, quite contrary, how does your (Madison Square) Garden grow? With disco balls and dance halls and screaming girls all in their rows.
body: Harry Styles first played Madison Square Garden at 18, as a heartthrob in a little pop quintet called One Direction. In 2012, he was fresh off Britain’s The X Factor and, not long before that, working the counter at W Mandeville Bakery in his native village of Holmes Chapel. He had a name—and an impish smile—ripe for stardom and a taste for skinny jeans. Arriving at the venue, he kissed the floor and marveled: “I made it to Madison Square Garden.”
These days, “I wouldn’t be caught dead kissing the floor with my pathetic immune system,” Styles told the crowd. “However, it is not lost on me what it means to play here.”

articles.title: How Endometriosis Symptoms Changed My Beauty Routine
articles.summary: More women than ever are being diagnosed with endometriosis. Easing symptoms means overhauling your lifestyle and adopting a broader view of beauty.
body: When I was finally diagnosed with endometriosis a few weeks shy of my 27th birthday — after more than a decade of debilitating pain, medical gaslighting and unanswered questions — I burst into tears. But the relief soon gave way to panic. Rather than just a reproductive issue, endometriosis is a whole-body condition, affecting everything from emotional regulation to hormone production and gut health. I had a sinking feeling my life was about to change: what I eat, how I manage stress, the kind of exercise I do, and even my beauty routine.

“Endometriosis is a body-wide metabolic dysfunction, which affects every organ system,” says Dr. Felice Gersh, a globally renowned women’s health specialist and medical director at the Integrative Medical Group of Irvine. “You will have more stress reactions and pain sensitization, and of course, living in pain alters everything from self-image to relationships to quality of life.”
points: More women than ever are being diagnosed with endometriosis.
Easing symptoms means overhauling your lifestyle and adopting a broader view of beauty.
